Mr. I. C. Herried August 10, 1973 Page 4
5. In light of the planning history related to the Airport Spur, the existence of other freeways already within the vicinity, the presence of airport and air generated ground and air travel, and the transitioning of land uses from agricultural to residential and industry in the vicinity of the airport, it is difficult to find that the Airport Spur will have an adverse environmental impact on the community which has already been subject to or constructed around major transportation facilities.
6. It should be noted that the regional transportation plan elements have been prepared and are maintained current under a continuing comprehensive planning process conducted by the Commission. The Commission's comprehensive planning program takes into account, on a broad scale, the impact upon the environment of all recommended public works improvements. In fact, all regional planning elements are prepared within the framework of a series of objectives, principles, and standards intended not only to provide necessary public facilities to serve existing and future development within the Region, but also to insure the preservation and enhancement of sustaining and underlying natural resource base of the Region. By design, then, the provision of the Airport Spur as recommended in adopted regional transportation plans was preceded by comprehensive planning efforts which took into account, among many other things, the impact on the regional environment of the proposed facility.
We trust that these comments are of help to you in the preparation of the final environmental statement relative to the Airport Spur within Milwaukee County, Wisconsin. Should you have any questions on this matter, please feel free to contact us.
Sincerely,
K. W. Bauer Executive Director
